reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g2_mg_q4_2), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale:
The sample set comprehensively fulfills the competency requirements across all three time scales and timetables. Elapsed minutes in an hour are assessed directly in items such as "A class started at 9:15 a.m. and ended at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes did it last?" (seed 42) and "A soccer practice started at 12:45 p.m. and ended at 1:35 p.m. How many minutes did it last?" (seed 46). Elapsed hours in a day are evaluated in items like "The train journey ended at 5:00 p.m. after running for 6 hours. What time did it start?" (seed 601) and "The train journey started at 10:00 a.m. and lasted for 5 hours. What time did it end?" (seed 605). Elapsed days in a week are tested in "A school sports meet begins on Thursday and finishes on Saturday of the same week. How many days does the school sports meet run?" (seed 45). Timetables and schedules are directly assessed in items like "Look at the bus timetable:
• Bus 1: Departs 7:00 a.m., Arrives 7:30 a.m.
• Bus 2: Departs 8:15 a.m., Arrives 9:05 a.m.
According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 1?" (seed 44) and "Look at the class schedule:
• Math: 8:00 a.m. – 9:00 a.m.
• English: 9:00 a.m. – 9:45 a.m.
How many minutes long is the English class?" (seed 50).

comprehensive_coverage.rationale:
The sample set provides full multi-directional coverage of elapsed time calculations. It includes finding duration given start and end times ("A movie started at 5:10 p.m. and ended at 5:50 p.m. How many minutes did it last?", seed 43), finding end time given start time and duration ("A soccer practice started at 10:25 a.m. and lasted 55 minutes. What time did it end?", seed 604; "The community sports festival started at 10:00 a.m. and lasted for 6 hours. What time did it end?", seed 603), finding start time given end time and duration ("The train journey ended at 5:00 p.m. after running for 6 hours. What time did it start?", seed 601), finding end day given start day and duration in days ("A 2-day school sports meet starts on Wednesday. On what day of the week does it end?", seed 501), and reading tabular schedules ("Look at the bus timetable:
• Bus 1: Departs 7:00 a.m., Arrives 7:45 a.m.
• Bus 2: Departs 8:15 a.m., Arrives 9:15 a.m.
According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 2?", seed 602).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All problems are well-calibrated to the developmental stage of Grade 2 Quarter 4 students. Contexts are familiar and relatable, including classes, sports meets, practices, movie watching, and bus/train trips. Wordings are concise and direct. Calculations involve manageable 5-minute increments (e.g., "A class started at 9:15 a.m. and ended at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes did it last?", seed 42) or single-digit whole hours and days within the same week, avoiding undue cognitive overload.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale:
A balanced distribution of formats and structural variants is present across the 15 seeds. Both multiple choice ('mcq') and numeric/fill-in-the-blank ('cloze') item types are utilized. The variants cover tabular timetable parsing ("Look at the bus timetable:
• Bus 1: Departs 7:00 a.m., Arrives 7:30 a.m.
• Bus 2: Departs 8:15 a.m., Arrives 9:05 a.m.
According to the timetable, how many minutes is the travel time for Bus 1?", seed 44), calendar day span arithmetic ("An art workshop begins on Wednesday and finishes on Saturday of the same week. How many days does the art workshop run?", seed 600), and forward/backward time computations across hours and minutes.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every item strictly adheres to the stated MATATAG competency text without introducing out-of-scope topics such as 24-hour notation, multi-week calendar navigation, or unit conversions between unlike units. All questions remain strictly bounded to elapsed minutes within an hour boundary, hours in a day, and days in a week as exemplified by "A soccer practice started at 12:45 p.m. and ended at 1:35 p.m. How many minutes did it last?" (seed 46) and "A school sports meet begins on Tuesday and finishes on Friday of the same week. How many days does the school sports meet run?" (seed 502).

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numerical values and intervals are appropriately scaled for Grade 2 arithmetic. Minute intervals range from 20 to 60 minutes with multiples of 5 ("A soccer practice started at 10:25 a.m. and lasted 55 minutes. What time did it end?", seed 604; "A class started at 9:15 a.m. and ended at 9:35 a.m. How many minutes did it last?", seed 42). Hour intervals are single-digit integers (5 to 6 hours), and day spans are between 2 and 4 days ("A 2-day school sports meet starts on Wednesday. On what day of the week does it end?", seed 501; "A school sports meet begins on Thursday and finishes on Saturday of the same week. How many days does the school sports meet run?", seed 45).
